Radar & Camera Calibration in Riyadh

Calibration of driver-assistance radar and camera systems in Riyadh after windscreen replacement, bodywork, alignment changes or ADAS warnings.

  1. Home
  2. Maintenance
  3. Radar & Camera Calibration

Adaptive cruise, lane keeping, collision warning and automatic braking all depend on sensors that must know exactly where they point. A windscreen replacement, bumper repair, suspension change or even a hard impact can leave a radar or camera physically fine but aimed wrongly — and a mis-aimed assistance system is worse than a disabled one. QSC calibrates these sensors to the vehicle's specification and verifies the systems afterwards.

Driver-assistance sensors are aimed like rifle scopes: a radar behind a bumper emblem, a camera behind the windscreen, each referenced to the vehicle's geometry within fractions of a degree. The systems using them make braking and steering decisions from that aim. After glass replacement, bumper work, suspension changes or a geometry-altering impact, the sensor may test electrically perfect while pointing measurably wrong — and a lane-keeping system working from wrong data is actively worse than one switched off. Calibration is the procedure that re-establishes trust between the sensor and the road.

The procedures themselves are unforgiving of shortcuts: static calibration demands precise target placement on a level floor with controlled lighting; dynamic calibration demands specific road conditions and speeds; many vehicles require both in sequence. QSC follows the manufacturer's defined procedure for each model and documents completion — paperwork that matters for insurance repairs and for your own record that safety systems were restored properly after bodywork.

FAQ

Frequently asked questions

I replaced my windscreen and there are no warnings. Do I still need calibration?

Often yes. A camera can be out of specification without triggering a fault — the system simply judges distances and lane positions slightly wrongly. If the manufacturer's procedure calls for calibration after glass replacement, it should be done.

Is calibration needed after wheel alignment?

On some platforms, yes — radar aim is referenced to the vehicle's thrust line. The workshop confirms the requirement for your model rather than applying one rule to all cars.

Can you calibrate after bodywork done elsewhere?

Yes. Bring the car with whatever repair documentation exists; QSC assesses sensor mounting and runs the correct procedure.

The shop that replaced my windscreen said calibration is unnecessary. Are they right?

Check what the manufacturer's procedure says for your model — for most camera-equipped vehicles, glass replacement explicitly requires calibration even when no warning appears. If the procedure requires it and it was skipped, the system's judgments are unverified. We can check the requirement for your exact vehicle in minutes.
